physicalCorrections.title: Physical build corrections (estimated)
physicalCorrections.stepOnePrompt: First, choose the spoke type that matches your hub.
physicalCorrections.stepThreePrompt: Enter the rim offset and alternating-drilling offset
physicalCorrections.stepThreeSubtitle: Continue with the rim's overall offset and the alternating left/right hole offset from the rim center reference.
physicalCorrections.stepFourPrompt: Enter hub PCD and WL / WR
physicalCorrections.stepFourSubtitle: Confirm the hub pitch circle diameter and the left/right flange distances to the wheel centerline.
physicalCorrections.stepFiveSubtitle: Confirm the flange hole diameter used to subtract the hole radius from the theoretical hole center; the measurement rule applies to both J-bend and straight-pull hubs.
physicalCorrections.stepSixSubtitle: Choose whether the spokes are interlaced at crossings for each wheel; if they are, enter the added length from the small bends.
physicalCorrections.pcdPairHelp: Enter the hub PCD, WL, and WR separately for the front and rear wheels.
physicalCorrections.flangeOrientationNote: Left and right follow the rider seated on the bicycle facing forward. Keep this orientation consistent with the hub maker's drawing.
physicalCorrections.frontFlangeSideNote: Left flange = disc side · Right flange = non-disc side
physicalCorrections.rearFlangeSideNote: Left flange = non-drive side (NDS) · Right flange = drive side (DS, freehub side)
physicalCorrections.alternatingPairHelp: Enter the front and rear alternating-drilling offsets separately; use 0 when the rim has no alternating drilling.
physicalCorrections.alternatingInputNote: A positive value moves the hole toward the left; a negative value moves it toward the right. Prefer the rim maker's specification.
physicalCorrections.rimOffsetInputNote: For an asymmetric rim, enter the rim bed's overall offset from the wheel centerline; use 0 for a symmetric rim. This is separate from the alternating-drilling offset.
physicalCorrections.holePairHelp: Enter the front and rear hub flange-hole diameters separately; common 14G spoke hubs are about 2.4–2.6 mm.
physicalCorrections.holeInputNote: Some hubs have no official CAD drawing, so the exact value cannot be confirmed directly. Some use a recessed counterbore or retention seat and some do not. Enter the actual hole value for J-bend; enter the value that matches the straight-pull structure. If official CAD already includes this detail, enter 0.
physicalCorrections.interlacingPairHelp: Set interlacing separately for the front and rear wheels, then enter the matching length compensation when enabled.
physicalCorrections.interlacingInputNote: With 2x / 3x lacing, pressing one spoke over or under another at the outer crossing creates a small bend. Turn this off when spokes are not interlaced.
physicalCorrections.erdPairHelp: Enter the front and rear rim ERD values separately.
physicalCorrections.erdInputHelp: Enter the measured ERD in millimetres.
physicalCorrections.jBendHint: The spoke forms a hook at the flange hole.
physicalCorrections.straightPullHint: The spoke exits the hub slot in a straight line with no J-shaped bend.

parameter.title: Parameter definitions
parameter.intro: Use these definitions to double-check your rim and hub data before calculating. Small measurement differences can change the spoke length.

erd.title: ERD (Effective Rim Diameter)
erd.desc: The diameter at the spoke nipple seats inside the rim. Use the rim brand's ERD spec or measure it with two nipples and a caliper.

flangeDiameter.title: Flange diameter
flangeDiameter.desc: The circle diameter through the spoke hole centers on the hub flange (left and right can be different).

centerToFlange.title: Center-to-flange
centerToFlange.desc: The distance from the hub centerline to each flange (left and right). This affects dish and spoke length asymmetry.

holeCount.title: Spoke hole count
holeCount.desc: Must match both rim and hub (e.g. 24/28/32). Make sure you select the same count for front and rear.

crossPattern.title: Cross pattern
crossPattern.desc: How many times each spoke crosses other spokes (2x/3x/4x). Higher cross typically increases spoke length.

parameter.note: Tip: If you are unsure, use the manufacturer's published specs. If you measure yourself, measure twice and enter values to the same unit (mm).

workflow.title: Spoke length workflow
workflow.overviewAlt: Overview illustration for calculating bicycle spoke length
workflow.overviewCaption: Overview illustration showing which rim and hub measurements are needed to calculate bicycle spoke length.
workflow.stepOneFormulaValue: ERD = spoke 1 length + spoke 2 length + measured distance
stepOneItems: Prepare two old spokes of known length, two nipples, and a caliper.
Insert spokes through opposite holes in the rim.
Screw nipples until flush with the nipple groove bottom (ideal final position).
workflow.stepOneNote: * This method compensates for rim manufacturing tolerances.
workflow.stepOneAlt: Diagram showing how Effective Rim Diameter (ERD) is measured
workflow.stepOneCaption: Diagram showing how Effective Rim Diameter (ERD) is measured using two spokes, nipples and a caliper.
workflow.flangeDiameterBody: Use calipers to measure the distance between opposing spoke hole centers on the same flange.
workflow.centerToFlangeBody: Remove the hub axle if needed. Measure from the flange center to the hub centerline (or locknut face and subtract).
workflow.stepThreeBody: Enter measurements into the calculator. If the result is between standard sizes (e.g. 288.4mm), you usually round to the nearest available 1mm increment.
workflow.tipBody: Being 1mm longer is generally safer than 1mm shorter to ensure full thread engagement.
